extracted.intended_audience: auditors, institutional financial aid administrators, and compliance officers responsible for Title IV student aid programs
extracted.subtask_description: Audit and compliance guidance for institutions and auditors covering Student Financial Assistance (Title IV) programs, including program limits, matching, reporting, verification, disbursement, refunds, and return-of-funds rules. Used to test institutional compliance with statutes and 34/42 CFR requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate loan limits for subsidized and unsubsidized loans
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate loan limits for subsidized and unsubsidized loans is $23,000 for a dependent undergraduate student; $46,000 for an independent student; and $138,500 ($65,500 subsidized and $73,000 unsubsidized) for a graduate or professional student (includes loans for undergraduate study).

rubrics_metrics.name: PLUS loan eligibility and limit
rubrics_metrics.description: PLUS loans are limited to parent borrowers. A PLUS loan may not exceed the student's estimated cost of attendance minus other financial aid awarded during the period of enrollment for that student (FFEL, 34 CFR sections 682.201 and 682.204; Direct Loan, 34 CFR sections 685.200 and 685.203).

rubrics_metrics.name: Perkins Loan institutional matching share (ICC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution's matching share (Institutional Capital Contribution (ICC)) is one third of the Federal Capital Contribution (FCC) (or 25 percent of the combined FCC and ICC) (34 CFR section 674.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: FSEOG federal share limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal share of awards may not exceed 75 percent of the total FSEOG awards made by the school. The Secretary may authorize 100 percent Federal funding if certain conditions are met (34 CFR section 676.21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Work Study (FWS) federal share limits and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, the Federal share of FWS compensation paid a student employed other than by a private for-profit organization may not exceed 75 percent of the total FWS awards made by the school. The Federal share may exceed 75 percent, but not exceed 90 percent, for up to ten percent of the students compensated by FWS during the academic year, if certain conditions are met. The Federal share of FWS for work at private-for-profit organizations is limited to 50 percent. A 100 percent Federal share is allowable in two specified situations involving eligible institutions or certain tutoring/family literacy employment (34 CFR section 675.26; 42 USC 2753(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions for exceeding 75%: student employed at eligible nonprofit/government agency not affiliated with institution, selected case-by-case, and who otherwise couldn't afford costs. Two 100%-share situations described in text — see regs for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: HPSL/PCL/NSL institutional matching share
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution's matching share (ICC) is one ninth of the FCC and must be deposited in a health professions student loan fund (42 CFR sections 57.202 and 57.302).

rubrics_metrics.name: FWS earmarking for community service
rubrics_metrics.description: An institution shall use at least 5 percent of its allocation for an award year to compensate students employed in community service activities unless waived by the Secretary. Beginning July 1, 2000, that percentage increases to 7 percent.

rubrics_metrics.name: FWS use of funds for JLD program limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution can only use up to 10 percent of its FWS or $50,000 whichever is less for a JLD program (34 CFR sections 675.18 and 675.32).

rubrics_metrics.name: Perkins program income reinvestment
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal and interest repayments made by students and reimbursements for canceled loans are reinvested in the Federal Perkins Loan revolving fund (34 CFR section 674.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: GAPS for grant administration and payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees draw funds and account to ED using GAPS. Grantees request funds by creating a payment request in the GAPS External Access System, calling the GAPS Payee Hotline, or submitting an SF-270 if on reimbursement. GAPS maintains cumulative data on net draws and available balances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ED considers drawn funds to have been expended by the grantee for the award(s) identified (grantee has up to three days to make disbursements). Grantees can adjust drawn amounts between grant awards in GAPS so net adjustment is zero. Auditors should reconcile internal records with GAPS Activity Report (available online/hard copy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pell Payment Data reporting timelines and processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must report student payment data (Pell Payment Data) to ED; institutions must report student payment data within 30 calendar days after the school makes a payment or becomes aware of the need to adjust previously reported data. ED returns Processed Payment Data categorized as Rejected, Accepted with Assumptions, Duplicates and Accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In testing, auditors should be most concerned with data ED categorized as Accepted or Accepted with Assumptions. Transition to RFMS origination and disbursement records described; batch systems being phased out (floppy disk recipient data exchange).

rubrics_metrics.name: FISAP annual submission and required line items
rubrics_metrics.description: FISAP (Fiscal Operations Report and Application to Participate) is submitted annually to receive campus-based funds; required to be submitted by October 1 following the end of the award year. Key line items include Part I Identifying Information; Part II Application (enrollment, assessments and expenditures, information on eligible aid applicants); Part III Federal Perkins Loan Program fiscal report (fund activity, cumulative repayment info, cohort default rate); Parts IV–VI sections for FSEOG, FWS, program summary, and distribution of recipients/expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FISAP is electronic (ED Form 646-1). Use the Trace material line items guidance in auditing these sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSLDS overpayment and loan history reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: FPL and grant overpayment reporting to the National Student Loan Data System (NSLDS) — NSLDS is a national database of loans and other Title IV aid; institutions and lending entities may enter data pertaining to overpayments. Individual loan histories and grant overpayment summaries are accessible; individual student identifier is SSN (20 USC 1092b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate funds for HPSL, NSL, FPL
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance Requirement: The institution must maintain a separate fund account for each program (HPSL, 42 CFR section 57.205; NSL, 42 CFR section 57.305; and FPL, 34 CFR sections 674.8 and 674.19).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit Objective: Determine whether separate fund account(s) were established. Suggested Procedure: Review accounting records to verify that separate fund was established for each program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of selected applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance Requirement: An institution shall require each applicant whose application is selected by the central processor, based on edits specified by ED, to verify the items specified in 34 CFR section 668.56. The institution is not required to verify applications of more than 30 percent of its total number of applicants. Institution shall require applicants to verify any information used to calculate EFC it has reason to believe is inaccurate and must have written policies/procedures incorporating 34 CFR section 668.53. Acceptable documentation is listed in 34 CFR 668.57.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit Objective: Determine whether the institution established policies and procedures to verify information and verified required information of selected applications. Suggested Procedures: (a) Review policies/procedures for compliance with 34 CFR 668.53. (b) Select a sample of applications that were selected for verification and review files to ascertain acceptable documentation was obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and conditions for disbursements to students (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance Requirement: The institution may not make a disbursement to a student for a payment period until the student is enrolled in classes for that payment period. The earliest an institution may disburse SFA funds other than FWS is 10 days before the first day of classes of the payment period, with two exceptions described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: (1) Institutions generally may not deliver first installment of FFEL or Direct Loans to first-year first-time undergraduates until 30 days after first day of classes, unless exempted for cohort default rate <10% over 3 years. (2) For clock hour programs or nonstandard terms, earliest disbursement is later of 10 days before first day or day student completed previous payment period, with FFEL/Direct exceptions in cited regs (34 CFR 668.164).

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Aid Transcript (FAT) requirement when student received aid elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: If a student received financial aid while attending other institutions, the financial aid administrator must request a financial aid transcript (FAT) from the other institutions or obtain info from NSLDS. Once FAT is requested, institution can pay Pell and campus-based aid for one payment period only and can certify FFEL or originate Direct loan, but cannot release loan proceeds or make subsequent payments until FAT is received (34 CFR section 668.19).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Dear Colleague Letter 96-13 for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification-selected applicant disbursement restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: For students selected for verification, if the institution has reason to believe application info is inaccurate, the institution may not: (1) disburse any Pell or campus-based aid; (2) employ the applicant in FWS; or (3) certify FFEL or originate Direct Loans until the applicant verifies or corrects info. If no reason to believe info inaccurate, institution may withhold payment or make limited disbursement and allow employment for first 60 consecutive days, and may certify/ originate loans but cannot process proceeds. If verification not complete after 45 days, institution shall return proceeds to lender (34 CFR section 668.58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pell disbursement eligibility and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: To disburse Pell funds, the institution must have received a valid ISIR from the central processor or a valid SAR from the student by the earlier of the deadline notice published in the Federal Register or the last date the student is still enrolled and eligible for payment. Institution must review and document the student's eligibility before it disburses funds each payment period (34 CFR sections 690.61, 690.75–690.78).

rubrics_metrics.name: FPL disbursement scheduling and promissory note
rubrics_metrics.description: If institution is making a loan for a full academic year and uses standard academic terms, it must advance a portion of the loan during each payment period. If standard academic terms are not used, it must advance funds at least twice during the academic year - once at the beginning and once at the midpoint. Loan payments must be supported by a signed promissory note (34 CFR section 674.16).

rubrics_metrics.name: FFEL continued eligibility and disbursement timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution must determine student has maintained eligibility for FFEL before each disbursement. Disbursements are required on a payment period basis and the institution must provide the lender with a disbursement schedule. Reimbursement-method institutions must receive Department approval prior to disbursing loan funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing restrictions for requesting/disbursing funds: EFT/master check requests may not be made earlier than 27 days after first day of classes for first-year first-time Stafford borrower; 13 days before first day for subsequent payment periods or other borrowers. Disbursement timelines after receipt: 10 business days (EFT/master check between July 1, 1997 and June 30, 1999), 3 business days (EFT/master check on or after July 1, 1999), 30 days if lender provided check payable to borrower or copayable to borrower and institution. If student doesn't register/withdraws/ institution fails to disburse in required timeframe, institution must return funds to lender within 10 business days (with exceptions per regs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Loan eligibility and promissory note/roster requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Before disbursing Direct Loan proceeds (except allowable late disbursement), institution must determine student maintained continuous eligibility from beginning of loan period. Option 1 and Option 2 institutions may not disburse until they have obtained a legally enforceable promissory note. Option 1 and standard origination institutions may only disburse funds for students listed on the Actual Disbursement Roster (34 CFR sections 685.301 and 685.303).

rubrics_metrics.name: HPSL/PCL/NSL borrower status and promissory note requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Student loans may be paid to or on behalf of student borrowers in installments appropriate to the school, but a school may not pay more than the school determines the student needs for any given installment period. HPSL borrower must be full-time; NSL borrower at least half-time. Each student loan must be evidenced by a properly executed promissory note (42 USC 292r(a)(2); HPSL 42 CFR 57.209; NSL 42 CFR 57.309; HPSL/NSL promissory note regs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective Nov 13, 1998 amount of loan may be increased in third/fourth year of medical school to pay balances of loans made for attendance at the school (statutory citation provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: FWS wage payment and account-crediting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The student's wages are earned when the work is performed. The institution shall pay the student at least once per month. The Federal share must be paid by check or similar instrument the student can cash on endorsement. Effective July 1, 2000, an institution may, upon request by a student, credit FWS funds to a student's account for tuition, fees, institutional room and board, and other school-provided goods and services (34 CFR section 675.16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit procedures for disbursements
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit Objective: Determine whether disbursements to students were made or returned to lenders in accordance with required time frames; and whether required reviews were made and documents/approvals obtained before disbursing SFA funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested Procedures: (a) Review a sample of disbursements to verify they were made/returned in required time frames and for Direct Loan Option 1/standard origination only to students listed on Actual Disbursement Roster. (b) Review loan or other files to verify required procedures/documents/approvals (e.g., Department approval for reimbursement method) were obtained prior to disbursing funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: School refund policy fairness and refund processing (Refunds methodology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance Requirement - 'Refunds': A school is required to have a fair and equitable refund policy under which the school shall make refunds of unearned tuition, fees, room and board and other charges to a student who received HEA Title IV Student Financial Assistance. Under FFEL, the school pays to the original lender (or subsequent holder) the portion of the refund allocable to the loan. Refunds should be processed in accordance with established time frames (34 CFR section 668.22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation rule: method to determine minimum refund amount
rubrics_metrics.description: The refund policy should provide for a refund of at least the larger of: (1) applicable State law; (2) standards of institution's nationally recognized accrediting agency if approved by Secretary; or (3) the statutorily defined pro rata refund calculation for any student attending the school for the first time and who withdrew on or before the 60 percent point in time of the period of enrollment. If pro rata does not apply and no State/accreditor standards exist, refund should be at least the larger of the Federal refund calculation or the school's policy used for non-SFA students (34 CFR section 668.22(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds of $25 or less
rubrics_metrics.description: Refunds of $25 or less may not have to be repaid. A school may retain a refund of $25 or less due to an SFA loan program only if the school has written authorization from the student in the enrollment agreement explaining that the student permits the school to keep the funds rather than have them reduce loan debt (34 CFR section 668.22(g)(3)(iii)(B)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro rata refund calculation and allowable deductions
rubrics_metrics.description: The pro rata refund means a refund of not less than the portion of charges equal to the portion of the period of enrollment that remains on the withdrawal date, rounded down to the nearest 10 percent of that period, less: (1) unpaid amount of scheduled cash payment; (2) reasonable administrative fee not to exceed the lesser of 5 percent of tuition/fees/room/board/other charges assessed or $100; and (3) documented costs of equipment issued to the student that is unreturnable or not returned in good condition (34 CFR section 668.22(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal refund calculation and tiered refund percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal refund calculation provides minimum refund percentages depending on withdrawal timing: (1) If withdraw before first day — program amounts considered overpayments and must be returned; (2) If institution can't document attendance — program amounts are overpayments and must be returned; (3) Withdraw on first day — refund 100% of institutional charges less admin fee up to lesser of 5% or $100; (4) Withdraw after first day up to 10% — refund at least 90% less admin fee; (5) After 10% up to 25% — at least 50% less admin fee; (6) After 25% up to 50% — at least 25% less admin fee (34 CFR section 668.22(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal date for calculating refunds is defined (see separate criterion). Allocation order for refunds to programs is specified (see allocation criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal date determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The withdrawal date is the earlier of: (a) the date the student notifies institution of withdrawal or date of withdrawal specified by student (whichever is later); or (b) if student drops out without notifying institution, the last recorded date of class attendance as documented. If institution required to take attendance, withdrawal date is last date of academic attendance determined from attendance records. If not required to take attendance, withdrawal date rules include date began withdrawal process, date of official notification, midpoint of payment period for unofficial withdrawal, institutional determination for illness/grievous loss, date student began approved LOA if not returning, or date student began unapproved LOA (34 CFR sections 668.22(b)-(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions required to take attendance are those required by an external entity (accrediting/state). See Federal SFA Handbook Chapter 3 for detailed guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation order of refunds to programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Refunds must be distributed in the prescribed order regardless of school's agreements: (1) Unsubsidized Federal Stafford Loan; (2) Subsidized Stafford; (3) Federal PLUS Loan; (4) Unsubsidized Federal Direct Stafford Loan; (5) Subsidized Federal Direct Stafford Loan; (6) Federal Direct PLUS Loan; (7) Federal Perkins Loan; (8) Federal Pell Grant; (9) FSEOG; (10) Other SFA Programs; (11) Other Federal/State/private/institutional sources; (12) The student. HEAL loan portion must be paid directly to the original lender or subsequent holder and borrowers notified (42 CFR section 60.54).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for refunds to SFA programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Refunds due to SFA programs (including Direct Loan) are required to be deposited to SFA accounts within 30 days or returned to the appropriate FFEL lender within 60 days of the date the student officially withdraws or is expelled, or the date institution determines student unofficially withdrew. For students who do not return from approved LOA refunds should be made within 30 days of earlier of end of LOA or date student notifies institution they will not be returning (34 CFR sections 668.22, 682.607, and 685.306).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 3 of the Federal SFA Handbook for detailed withdrawal date determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of Funds methodology (post-withdrawal calculation and disbursement rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance Requirement - Return of Funds: Institution must determine amount of Title IV aid earned by student as of withdrawal date. If earned amount is less than disbursed amount, difference must be returned to Title IV programs. If earned is greater than disbursed, difference is a post-withdrawal disbursement. Post-withdrawal disbursements must be made from available grant funds before loan funds. Post-withdrawal disbursements may be credited to student's account for outstanding charges up to amount of outstanding charges. If loan funds are used to credit account, institution must notify student/parent and provide opportunity to cancel all or a portion of the loan. Institutions must offer, by written notification, post-withdrawal disbursements not credited to account within 30 days of institution's determination of withdrawal (34 CFR sections 668.22(a)(1)-(4) and 668.164(g)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If institution implements new return-of-funds regulations early, must implement entire methodology for all Title IV students and cannot revert back to old methodology. New regs effective July 1, 2000; implementation required by Oct 7, 2000; discretionary implementation on or after Nov 1, 1999, with restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of Title IV assistance earned (percentage earned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amount of earned Title IV grant or loan assistance is calculated by determining percentage of Title IV assistance earned as of withdrawal date: student earns 100% if withdrawal date is after completion of 60% of payment period/period of enrollment (credit hours or clock hours). Otherwise, percentage earned equals percentage of payment period/period of enrollment completed as of withdrawal date. Unearned amount is the complement and returned (34 CFR section 668.22(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of payment period vs. period of enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of Title IV funds if student withdraws must be determined on a payment period basis for standard term-based programs. For non-term based or nonstandard term-based programs, treatment may be determined on either a payment period basis or a period of enrollment basis (34 CFR section 668.22(e)(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of percentage of period completed (credit hours and clock hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: For credit-hour programs: percentage completed = calendar days completed / total calendar days in payment period (exclude schedule breaks of ≥5 consecutive days). For clock-hour programs: divide total clock hours in period into clock hours completed or scheduled to be completed as of withdrawal date if completed hours are at least 70% of scheduled hours. Total calendar days includes all days within period except scheduled breaks ≥5 days (34 CFR section 668.22(f)).
